```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(here)

# Load data
city_change <- read_csv(
  here("data", "clean", "city_change.csv")
)

# Visualize the lawsuit data
histogram_year <- ggplot(city_change) +
  aes(x = firstyr) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Fist Year of A Fair Housing Lawsuit by City",
    x = "Year of Lawsuit",
    y = "Number of Cities"
  )

# visualize the white share data
histogram_white <- ggplot(city_change) +
  aes(x = change_white) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = .025 )+
  labs(
    title = "Percent Change in a City's Population that is Non-Hispanic White",
    x = "Percent",
    y = "Number of Cities"
  )

# Descriptive statistics
summary <- summary(city_change |>
                     select(
                       firstyr,
                       white_initial,
                       white_2010,
                       change_white
                     ), na.rm = TRUE)
range <- max(city_change, na.rm = TRUE) - min(city_change, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(city_change$change_white, na.rm = TRUE)
sdy<- sd(city_change$firstyr, na.rm = TRUE)
sdw1<- sd(city_change$white_initial, na.rm = TRUE)
sdw2 <- sd(city_change$white_2010, na.rm = TRUE)
sdw3 <- sd(city_change$change_white, na.rm = TRUE)
mediany <- median(city_change$firstyr, na.rm = TRUE)
medianw1<- median(city_change$white_initial, na.rm = TRUE)
medianw2 <- median(city_change$white_2010, na.rm = TRUE)
medianw3 <- median(city_change$change_white, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Presentation Overview

This presentation has three components to it

- What the dataset is
- A paper that used the data set
- Research Extensions of the Paper's dataset

## The Dataset

- This dataset motivated me because it contributes directly to my emerging research agenda on the work of regional intergovernmental organizations (RIGOs)
- My emerging conception of the function of these RIGOS is in their capacity to address externalities and spill overs produced by city land-use policies
- In this article, Trounstine examines how land use policies affect changes in racial demographics over time

## The Codebook

- The code book within this study is more accessible than most, as Trounstine provided the files on the Harvard Dataverse
- Her study posts documentation of the analyses run to produce the tables as well as the replication files
- However, some analytical choices are readily identifiable from the codebook alone and transporting it to R created some consistency problems in replication.
  - For example, it was not clear what the municipality identifier was.

## The Variables

- Fair Housing Act Injunction
  - A binary variable of whether a city had a Fair housing lawsuit
  - A secondary variable of the year of a city's first Fair housing lawsuit
  - This variable captures an event, a Fair Housing Lawsuit
  - The variable was hand-coded from a search of Fair Housing Documents
- Demographic data for all incorporated cities in metropolitan areas from 1968 to 2011
  - This is city year data that captures an attribute
  - The data come from the Decennial census
  - This variable is meant to capture the share of the city population that is white

## Descriptive Statistics

- First of onset of FHA lawsuit
  - Some multimodality,
  - A small peak in the early 1970s, and late 80s
  - Larger peaks in the mid-90s and 2000 to 2010
  - Median year of 1990
- White Share
  - Initial white share median 71.6%
  - White share in 2010 62.4%
  - Change in white share -5.8%
  - The data are highly left skewed, with large negative values and most values hovering around -5%

## The Paper

- The paper using this data set is Jessica Trounstine's "The Geography of Inequality: How Land Use Regulation Produces Segregation"
- This paper was motivated by the research linking residential zoning and segregation.
- The author used the onset of Fair Housing Lawsuits a natural experiment to test the relationship
- IV: Whether or not a city has an FHA lawsuit and the year
- DV: share of the white population in 2010
- The research question asks what the relationship is between the a city's strictness of land use and level of segregation.
- The paper finds about a five percent reduction in the city's percentage of whiteness, relative to cities thad did not experience an FHA lawsuit

## Extension

- How did metropolitan white share change as a result of changes in local land use resulting from FHA lawsuits?
- Do nonwhite property owners support stringent land use?
  - It appears that the research paper omits homeownership land-use preferences by race.
  - A major component of the argument of the paper is that homeowners seek to defend against reductions in property value by keeping housing scarce.
- I would like additional literature on how other planning entities mediate the changes in the share of white population
  - states, through direct preemption, and RIGOs through services, normative framing, and agenda setting may influence zoning patterns
